Visualizing the Mathematics Behind Machine Learning.

MathCore explains the mathematics behind modern NLP from first principles. Each topic combines step-by-step derivations with interactive visualizations and models you can run directly in your browser.

Read
Complete derivations

Every mathematical result is derived and not just thrown at you. You can see where each formula comes from with step by step explanations.

Drive
Instruments, not pictures

Each figure is computed live. You can drag points, sweep sliders, retrain models, and really visualize the math.

Check
Quick checks

Short quizzes after each idea, with an explanation for every option, right or wrong.

LM
Language Models

From counting words to training transformers: probability, gradients, embeddings, attention, and the models built on them.

AC
Advanced Concepts

Alignment, retrieval, translation, recurrent architectures, and speech: topics that build on the core language-model material but stand on their own.

Computational Linguistics
is being built.

Structure and meaning: tagging and sequence labeling, constituency and dependency parsing, semantic roles, coreference, and discourse. This volume is being written to the same standard as the rest of the site, which means every parser gets a chart you can step through and every algorithm gets a derivation rather than a citation.

About
this project

MathCore is an interactive guide to the mathematics behind modern natural language processing and machine learning. The focus is simple: visualizations you can manipulate and models you can run. Every core idea is paired with a visualization you can manipulate and a model you can run and experiment with, right in the browser.

Train a tiny neural network and watch it learn. Drag points across a decision boundary. Generate text one token at a time and see the probabilities shift. Everything is derived from first principles, so each result is something you can reconstruct rather than recall. The goal is working understanding, not a list of equations.

MathCore is built on a simple belief: the mathematics of machine learning should be open to anyone willing to look closely, not gated behind dense notation or a price tag. This site is my attempt to widen that access, and to reimagine these ideas as something you can see and touch rather than only read. Its range of topics draws on Speech and Language Processing by Daniel Jurafsky and James H. Martin as a reference point, but the vision, the visualizations, and the voice are my own.
